claims.claim: The name 'tomorrow' comes from how we count days.
claims.note: The word tomorrow comes from Old English roots meaning 'on the morning', not from counting days.

claims.claim: We start counting at one, and then we count through two, three, four, and so on.
When we get to ten, instead of saying it was yesterday, we say 'tomorrow'.
claims.note: Tomorrow is not related to the number ten; it refers to the day after today.

claims.claim: Tomorrow is the day that follows right after today.
Your heart works around the clock to pump blood throughout your circulatory system.
The heart delivers oxygen and nutrients to every cell in your body.
The heart removes waste products like carbon dioxide.
Without your heart beating steadily, you wouldn't survive long at all.
A toy car drives and moves along the road.
Ladybugs pollinate flowers.
Months were originally based on how long it takes for the Earth to complete its orbit around the Sun and our revolution relative to the fixed stars.
claims.note: Months were originally based on the Moon's phases, not Earth's orbit around the Sun.

claims.claim: The ancient Egyptians created the original calendar system we use today.
claims.note: Our modern Gregorian calendar derives primarily from the Roman Julian and Gregorian calendars, not the ancient Egyptian one.

claims.claim: The ancient Egyptians divided the year into twelve months.
The Romans initially had five months that didn't align with the seasons (March, May, July, August, and October).
claims.note: The early Roman calendar originally had 10 months, and the months listed do not match this historical structure.

claims.claim: Julius Caesar introduced the Julian calendar that standardized the number of days in each month.
This caused slight variations between the calendar's calculated dates and the actual astronomical cycles of the Earth over time.
We added an extra day to February every four years to make up the lost days when we used the solar year as a base.
Electric cars run on batteries instead of gas
They use electricity to spin a motor
They don't give off smoke
They don't make loud honking noises
claims.note: Electric cars can still honk their horns just like regular cars; they do not lack honking noises.

claims.claim: They help keep the air clean for everyone
Planes fly high up in the sky because they have powerful engines that push them forward
Planes have special wings that make them lift off the ground
Flying is like having a giant invisible carpet on air so they can zip across the whole world really fast
The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter.
Jupiter is way bigger than all the other planets put together.
A beat is the steady, regular sound you tap your foot to, like when someone claps or drums.
Rhythm is the fun, bouncing feel you move to, where your body shakes, jumps, or swings along.
Beat is what keeps everything swinging in time.
Rhythm is all the cool movements you do while listening.
claims.note: Rhythm is a pattern of sounds and rests in music, not the physical movements made while listening.

claims.claim: Longer trains have more cars, which means they can carry a lot more people and goods without adding extra fuel costs.
claims.note: Longer and heavier trains do require significantly more fuel and more powerful locomotives or additional engines to pull them.

claims.claim: The weight of a longer train helps distribute its load evenly, making it safer for the tracks and the infrastructure.
claims.note: Distributing weight across many axles can reduce point loads, though very long trains can also create high in-train forces and dynamic stress on tracks.

claims.claim: Trains travel on fixed rails, not rubber tires, which makes them stable over longer distances.
A pumpkin is usually orange.
A pumpkin gets its orange color from the sun.
claims.note: Pumpkins get their orange color from pigments called carotenoids as they ripen, not directly from the sun coloring them.

claims.claim: Singing while washing your hair helps to make sure you get all the soap and water out of your hair.
claims.note: Singing does not help remove soap or water from hair.

claims.claim: Singing is a way to help wash things away without needing a brush or a towel.
claims.note: Singing does not wash anything away and cannot replace a brush or towel.

claims.claim: Berries are yummy and full of healthy vitamins.
claims.note: Berries contain essential vitamins and nutrients.

claims.claim: They help keep our bodies strong and give us energy to play and grow big and tall.
claims.note: Eating nutritious foods like berries supports growth and provides energy.

claims.claim: New Year's Day on January 1st was originally established by Julius Caesar in 45 BCE as the beginning of the Roman calendar year.
The beginning of the Roman calendar year aligned with the agricultural cycle.
claims.note: January 1st did not align with the agricultural cycle; it was chosen because it was the date elected Roman magistrates entered office.

claims.claim: Emperor Julian decreed that it would be celebrated again in 46 BCE when he changed the calendar system.
claims.note: Emperor Julian lived in the 4th century CE and did not change the calendar in 46 BCE; Julius Caesar introduced the Julian calendar starting in 45 BCE (with 46 BCE being the transition year).

claims.claim: Because of this historical shift, we now have two New Year's celebrations: one in January and another on April 1st (April Fools' Day).
claims.note: April Fools' Day is not a second New Year's celebration caused by a calendar shift.

claims.claim: Ice floats because it is made of water
claims.note: Ice is made of water, but everything made of water does not necessarily float in water; the reason ice floats is its lower density relative to liquid water.

claims.claim: At 0°C, water molecules slow down and form a rigid crystal structure called hexagonal ice lattice
The hexagonal ice lattice takes up slightly more space than liquid water
When you drop a block of ice in water, it displaces its own volume of water
claims.note: An object displaces a volume of water equal to the volume of the submerged portion of the object, not its total volume.

claims.claim: Displacing water creates a buoyant force that lifts it off the bottom
Using energy-efficient appliances reduces your carbon footprint.
Turning off lights and electronics when you're not using them reduces your carbon footprint.
Walking, biking, or taking public transit instead of driving alone reduces your carbon footprint.
Reducing, reusing, and recycling your waste helps keep things out of landfills and saves energy.
A banana tastes sweet.
A banana tastes crunchy.
claims.note: Bananas are soft and creamy when ripe, not crunchy.

claims.claim: The air inside a standard blown-up balloon is lighter than the air outside.
claims.note: The air inside a blown-up balloon is actually denser and heavier than the surrounding air due to being under pressure, and normal breath-filled balloons do not float.

claims.claim: Balloons go up high in the sky because the air inside is lighter than the air outside.
claims.note: Balloons float because they are filled with a gas lighter than air like helium, or hot air, not because normal breath-filled air is lighter.

claims.claim: Friends make us feel happy because they care about us
Friends laugh along with us when we giggle
Friends give us kind words that make our heart smile
Having a budget helps you track your spending.
Having a budget helps you avoid overspending.
Having a budget helps you save money towards goals like buying a car or saving for college.
Having a budget gives you control over your money so you can plan ahead.
It is completely normal to feel scared of the dark.
As we grow up, our brains start building stronger connections between different parts.
Galaxies are huge collections of billions to trillions of stars, as well as gas and dust, held together by gravity.
Most of the matter in a galaxy is not made of familiar atoms like carbon or iron; instead, it's mostly dark matter.
Dark matter is only detected because it exerts gravitational pull on visible light.
claims.note: Dark matter is detected through its gravitational pull on visible matter (like stars and gas) and light (gravitational lensing), not just on visible light.

claims.claim: The stars in a galaxy form complex structures like spiral arms.
Some galaxies also have supermassive black holes at their centers.
Mixing blue and yellow together gives you yellow.
claims.note: Mixing blue and yellow makes green, not yellow.

claims.claim: Flowers are colorful plants that grow in gardens and parks
Flowers make us feel happy because they smell sweet and look pretty
Food becomes spicy because it contains compounds called capsaicinoids, which are found in chili peppers.
When you eat capsaicinoids, they bind to special pain sensors in your tongue and nose called TRPV1 receptors.
TRPV1 receptors send signals to your brain that make you feel heat rather than just taste bitterness.
The feeling of spice is your body's way of telling you that the food is hot.
Allergies happen when your immune system gets confused and thinks something harmless like pollen, dust, or certain foods is a real threat.
The immune system releases chemicals that cause symptoms like a runny nose, itchy eyes, and trouble breathing.
Having a family history of allergies puts you at higher risk.
You can build up immunity if you avoid the things that trigger them.
claims.note: Avoiding triggers does not build up immunity; rather, allergen avoidance prevents allergic reactions, while immunotherapy (allergy shots) is used to build tolerance.

claims.claim: Butterflies fly to find yummy flowers to eat.
Butterflies use their long tongues to sip sweet nectar from the flowers.
Day and night happen because the Earth is spinning like a giant top.
As the Earth spins, one half turns away from the sun getting dark, and the other half faces the sun getting bright.
Rainbows happen when raindrops catch some of the sunlight and bend it.
Rainbows make all the colors mix together in the sky.
claims.note: Rainbows separate or split sunlight into individual colors rather than mixing them together.

claims.claim: Yucky smells can happen when food mixes with air and gets warm.
Playing outside on a hot day makes the grass smell fresh and green.
Eating something too quickly makes it taste a bit funny.
